title: Understanding Trap Seal Integrity and Siphonage
description: Every fixture drain relies on a liquid trap seal, typically between two to four inches deep, to block sewer gases from entering living spaces. A common issue is trap siphonage, which occurs when a flowing drain creates negative pressure downstream, pulling the water seal out of the trap if it is not properly vented. To protect the trap seal, ensure the trap arm length meets code minimums and is correctly vented before drops occur. Inspecting and maintaining proper trap arm slope prevents self-siphonage and keeps the water barrier intact.

To protect the trap seal, ensure the trap arm length meets code minimums and is correctly vented before drops occur. Inspecting and maintaining proper trap arm slope prevents self-siphonage and keeps the water barrier intact.
